raw.assessment: The incumbent is plausibly adequate for stable courses: unchanged-assignment files had seven-minute median handling, and the documented CSV remains necessary. Assignment changes accompanied six affected exports, supporting investigation of week-specific selection without establishing causation. Two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account. Fast job execution and long replacement waits suggest a separate delay, but waiting is not measured handling. No sampled cross-center rows establishes only sample performance; course splits were untested.

openings.claim: Selection or reconciliation based on current instructor assignments and mutable course names may disagree with the intended week; resolving course identity and effective dates may prevent some affected exports.
openings.delta: Explains why the incumbent can work for stable assignments while explicitly testing renamed courses as a limiting case for assignment-only repair.
openings.prediction: In fabricated paired cases, changing only assignment timing alters exported membership if temporal selection is responsible. Changing only the course name distinguishes identity-sensitive selection from instructor-only behavior; unchanged membership with coordinator disagreement points elsewhere.
openings.probe: Replay unchanged, reassigned, and renamed fixtures in staging against a coordinator-agreed weekly course set. Compare selected course identities before CSV rendering and coordinator matching afterward. Add a fabricated split with center ownership checks; exercise concurrent attendance entry. Time-box investigation within six engineer-days using existing hosting and schema.
assumptions: A weekly intended course set can be agreed independently of current labels.
Historical assignment data or suitable stable identities may be unavailable; a production repair remains conditional on feasibility.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling primarily come from reconciling course lists, requesting replacements, or importing otherwise usable CSVs?
openings.delta: Separates the handling-time target from replacement turnaround and tests whether export-selection repair addresses the main labor cost.
openings.prediction: Reconciliation dominance produces longer checks on changed-course cases; import dominance persists with confirmed correct course sets. Replacement delays can remain long while consuming little active handling.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators’ two short sessions to time checking, downloading, replacement requests, and importing separately with fabricated CSVs and matched timetables. Record idle waiting separately. Retain the documented schema, existing hosting, and normal attendance entry; share the six-day investigation budget.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate ordinary workflows; the next 40 real exports are still required to evaluate the success measure.

raw.assessment: The sample misses both handling-time and course-set targets. Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but neither the selection mechanism nor the cause of handling time is established. One opening is warranted; feasibility within six engineer-days remains unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: presenting a requested week through current assignments and names generates reconciliation demand. If replacements repeat that resolution against a moving present, export discrepancies can cause retries that create further discrepancies. Replace this dependency with a center-specific, week-specific course manifest confirmed once and reused for replacements.
openings.delta: Counterfactual branch: forbid current instructor assignment as the authority for historical course membership. Change the export interface to accept stable course identities plus week-specific display labels, showing unresolved membership before generation. The former dependency's obligations are course inclusion, instructor relevance to the week, understandable labels, and center ownership. The manifest and confirmation must discharge each explicitly. This hybrid combines an explicit course-set contract with the existing CSV generator; their interaction holds membership steady while attendance values can refresh under a stated cutoff.
openings.prediction: With the same intended timetable, changing only current assignment or course name should leave manifest-based membership unchanged. Fewer repeated membership discrepancies would support the feedback hypothesis; unchanged discrepancies would weaken it. Any confirmation effort must count toward handling time.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two sessions for counterbalanced fabricated baseline and manifest exports, covering reassignment, rename, split courses, and another center. Record total handling and component times, intended membership, and replacement requests. Verify documented CSV import and concurrent attendance entry. If feasible within the cap, evaluate the next 40 exports against all stated targets.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: tenant-scoped stable course identities; persisted weekly manifests; authorized coordinator confirmation; sufficiently reliable weekly schedule evidence; explicit instructor and label information where needed; existing CSV serialization; nonblocking attendance reads and an explicit cutoff.
All participant processing stays in the private service and authorized workspace. Existing capabilities must support the change within six engineer-days and the hosting allowance; this is unverified.

critiques.assumption: A confirmed weekly course set remains a reliable authority for replacements.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 establishes heterogeneous timetables; their completeness and update timing are unmeasured. Confirmation may freeze an omission or obsolete split interpretation. This is an untested authority dependency, not an observed manifest failure.
critiques.opening: Make confirmed membership explicitly correctable, with revisions confined to disputed courses.
critiques.comparison: A1 stabilizes membership but may preserve mistakes; Z1 can resolve temporal identity but cannot establish timetable completeness. A correction path addresses a different dependency: revising intended membership after new information.
critiques.probe: Proposed: introduce a late timetable correction after confirmation and compare frozen versus revised membership, including all correction labor.

critiques.assumption: Replacement retries create additional discrepancies and materially increase active handling.
critiques.limitation: D1-O5 supplies turnaround delays, not changing replacement contents; D1-O7 lacks action recordings. The proposed feedback mechanism is unestablished.
critiques.opening: Gate a persistent manifest implementation on evidence of its incremental benefit.
critiques.comparison: Z2 separates active labor from waiting; A1 needs additional evidence that stable membership improves either labor or correctness.
critiques.probe: Proposed: compare baseline, frozen manifest, and correctable manifest on matched fabricated tasks; measure membership errors and active handling separately from waiting.

openings.claim: Reuse confirmed weekly membership until an explicit correction creates a new version.
openings.delta: Add targeted revision to A1 instead of treating one confirmation as permanently authoritative.
openings.prediction: Manifest reuse plus targeted correction should preserve repeatability while recovering late omissions. Unlike the existing generator alone, it retains approved membership; unlike frozen A1, it can amend errors. Their interaction is conditional reuse. Failure boundary: an undetected timetable error remains wrong.
openings.probe: Proposed only: assess one fabricated correction with six coordinators across two short sessions, retaining CSV import and concurrent entry. Count confirmation and revision time. Subsequent evaluation requires the next 40 exports and all original targets.
assumptions: Smallest capability: private staging preview of tenant-scoped course IDs, one correction, and regenerated documented CSV; stable IDs and correction authority require inspection.
Total first change stays within six engineer-days and existing hosting; participant names remain private, center ownership is enforced, and attendance entry continues.
